material_findings.title: PrivacyTrace: tool-call traces can leak inferred user attributes
material_findings.code_license: To be specified in author README; data license also to be specified, dataset access requires manual approval
material_findings.summary: Author paper describes 1,000 synthetic profiles, 4,000 agent trajectories and 25 MCP servers; reports 26.25% user-profile inference success from tool-call traces versus 17.97% prior-based guessing. The primary abstract and project README/DATA_CARD were independently opened, but no experiment was reproduced. The README explicitly says license to be specified, and dataset download requires author approval. Treat privacy leakage as a design/review concern, not a proven exploit in this repository.
material_findings.next_action: Build/integration agent: review whether source reports, tool-call logs and Agent Operations expose user-derived tool arguments/results; design a synthetic local fixture testing log minimization and cross-session linkage. Do not import the external code/dataset until explicit licensing and dataset access terms are verified; avoid real personal data.

material_findings.title: Simple Features Beat Most AI Control Monitors: benchmark shortcut and label-validity warning
material_findings.code_license: MIT for repository code/generated data; upstream datasets separately licensed
material_findings.summary: Author paper reports a simple bag-of-words baseline AUROC 0.806, above 20 of 24 previously evaluated open-weight monitor models, and identifies authorship/problem-metadata shortcuts plus invalid backdoor labels. This does not prove published monitors exploit the shortcuts. Primary paper and author README/LICENSE inspected; reported metrics and benchmark validity not independently reproduced.
material_findings.next_action: Build/integration agent: coordinate with Nov 2 morning PR #235 detector evaluation; build a small synthetic same-author/label-validity test and report precision at realistic base rates before treating any monitor benchmark score as assurance. Review third-party dataset terms; do not execute external untrusted code by default.
